text:
Matt Coronato ended it 4:08 into overtime, a snap shot off a feed from Matvei Gridin that sent the Saddledome home with a 4-3 win over PHI. It was the second time that night Calgary had to climb back, and the more dramatic of the two comebacks came from a penalty kill. Joel Farabee, drafted 14th overall by Philadelphia in 2018, scored shorthanded in the third period against the club that picked him, a backhander that tied it at 3-3. Our numbers say that goal was a 42 percent chance, the likeliest of any score in the game.

The game was played in waves. PHI controlled the second period, out-chancing CGY 1.70 to 0.52 in expected goals (a measure of the quality of shots taken). Noel Acciari's tip-in and Owen Tippett's power-play goal built a 3-2 lead, even as Zach Whitecloud pulled Calgary level on a 3 percent chance. Then the third period flipped completely: CGY won it 1.75 to 0.35 in expected goals. Devin Cooley stopped 32 of 35 shots, and Dan Vladar allowed four on 26. Our simulations of every shot gave CGY 54 percent to win, so the result was fair, if narrow.

The win gives Calgary a night to build on, with Coronato, the 13th pick in 2021, delivering the decisive goal and Farabee leading all forwards with five shots on goal. For Philadelphia, it is a lost point after taking the lead three separate times. Our data says PHI had its best stretch in the middle period and had no answer once Calgary pushed back. Our records feed doesn't include standings, so we'll leave the rest to the table.
